findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py `friction_reason` raises QueueError when `red_gate` is None, has no name, or has no cause/evidence. `_transition` calls `emit_friction(..., previous.get('red_gate'), ...)` on every no-change re-observation for states in `_FRICTION_STATES`. A blocked-escalation or repair state recorded earlier without a red gate, or with one that has no evidence, now raises on each pass. That could stall the transition and its label/escalation repair instead of degrading to a withheld event.
findings.summary: A friction-state transition now hard-fails when no red gate with a cause or evidence is available. That includes the idempotent re-observation path for already-published states, so one gate-less state can block the queue on every observation.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/finish_task.py `record_lifecycle_friction`: the argument list is built with `run_git(['rev-parse','HEAD'], cwd=root).stdout.strip()`, outside any try. If `run_git` raises (it may check the return code), the exception escapes. In `run_checks` that happens before `raise SystemExit(returncode)`, so the original validation exit code is replaced by a traceback. The same applies to the OpenSpec hygiene path.
findings.summary: `record_lifecycle_friction` is documented as best-effort and not changing the delivery outcome. It now runs an unguarded `git rev-parse HEAD` before the subprocess call.
